title: max-autotune compile (compile time is untimed)
description: One line: model = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, mode="max-autotune-no-cudagraphs"). val_bpb 0.988407 at 493.6M tokens, 1883 steps, MFU 34.85%, VRAM 49.7GB, total_seconds 488.8 (vs 325.4 baseline, i.e. +163s of untimed compile).
reflection: The accounting arbitrage is real but the payoff is small. total_training_time only accumulates from step 11, so the +163s of autotuning cost nothing against the 5 minutes and left ~410s of slack under the 900s harness timeout; it bought +2.3% tokens (482.4M control mean -> 493.6M) and +0.8 points of MFU (34.07 -> 34.85). Token-corrected at the within-cluster slope the quality residual is +0.0002, i.e. zero, exactly as predicted for a change that alters no math - the whole -0.0012 vs the control pair mean is throughput. My forecast of +6-10% tokens was 3x too optimistic: inductor's defaults were already close to optimal for this graph, and most of the 65% gap to peak MFU is FA3 at window 256 plus unavoidable logits traffic, neither of which the autotuner can touch. Cost side: peak VRAM 45.0 -> 49.7GB (autotuned kernel workspaces). Compile flags are now a closed axis - a second probe would be worth well under a thousandth of bpb.
